newsitem.title: HUNGARY: March maize futures dominate Hungary trade.
newsitem.headline: March maize futures dominate Hungary trade.

text.p: Maize futures for the March delivery dominated trade in the grains section of the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE), dealers said on Tuesday.
Those who sought to close their March positions were willing to go higher than the physical market would normally dictate, they added.
"Closing March contracts slightly higher still leaves them with a sizeable profit," said Tamas Kobulniczky of Swap."They opened those contracts at between 24,000 and 27,000 forints".
Maize for the March delivery closed at 19,590 forints, up 40 while the May delivery ended at 19,000 forints, down 200. Other maturities were steady.
March delivery maize accounted for 330 contracts out of a total 863 contracts or 375.1 million forints grain futures turnover.
Milling wheat prices finished lower for March, May and August maturities, December went up while other maturities remained unchanged.
Traders said new (1997) crop milling wheat prices are likely to remain speculative in the short term as it was too early for a realistic crop estimate.
"Worries about possible sleet damage to the wheat crop were exaggerated," Kobulniczky said. "A few bad spring days could do more damage than any amount of (January) sleet".
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
